title: Structures, members and member access
learningObjectives: Define a structure type using struct and named members.
Access members with the dot operator.
Explain structure assignment and member type constraints.
Use structures to model related data with a clear invariant.

understand.concept: A structure type groups named members into one object. Members can have different types, and each member is accessed through the containing structure. A structure definition describes a type; declaring an object creates storage for a value of that type. C supports structure assignment between compatible structure types but not built-in whole-structure equality comparison.
understand.whyItMatters: Structures model records such as products, coordinates and users while keeping related fields together under one object name.
understand.analogy: Treat the operation as a clearly specified contract between the program and its data.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace C's type, lifetime, I/O and object representation rules.

explain.narrative:
## 1. Define a structure

A `struct` declaration introduces a structure type and its named members. Each member has its own declared type.

## 2. Declare objects

Declare structure objects using the struct tag or a typedef alias. Members can be initialized in declaration order with an initializer list.

## 3. Access members

Use the dot operator, as in `item.price`, to access a member through a structure object. The expression has the member's declared type.

## 4. Assignment and comparison

Compatible structure objects can be assigned, copying member values. C does not provide `==` for complete structure objects; compare the relevant members explicitly.

## 5. Model valid data

Group values that belong together and define invariants, such as a quantity being nonnegative. Validate external data before storing it in a structure.
